title: When Silence Speaks Across Cultures
subtitle: 沉默并非没有意义：理解不同文化中的停顿、尊重与沟通信号。

sections.label: Reading
sections.title: 英语短文
sections.heading: When Silence Speaks Across Cultures
paragraphs: Imagine a meeting in which a manager asks for opinions and nobody answers immediately. One person may interpret the silence as a lack of preparation. Another may see it as a respectful pause that gives everyone time to think. Neither reaction is universal; each is shaped by conversational norms learned over many years.

In some cultures, quick responses convey confidence and help people build rapport. A pause that lasts several seconds may create discomfort, so speakers naturally fill it. In other cultures, interrupting a moment of silence can seem impatient. Careful listeners may wait before replying because they want their words to be accurate and considerate.

Silence can also communicate an implicit message. It may signal disagreement, uncertainty, respect for authority, or simply concentration. The difficulty is that the same behavior can carry opposite meanings in different settings. When people assume that their own interpretation is obvious, a quiet moment can easily become a source of mistrust.

Cross-cultural competence therefore requires curiosity rather than certainty. If a pause feels unusual, withhold judgment and look for additional clues: facial expressions, the relationship between speakers, and what happens next. You can also ask a neutral question such as, “Would you like a moment to think?” By making room for different communication styles, groups can turn silence from a barrier into a useful part of conversation.

items.pattern: The same behavior can be interpreted as A or B, depending on...
items.explanation: 同一种行为可能被理解为 A 或 B，取决于……。被动语态 be interpreted as 强调行为所获得的不同解读；depending on 补充决定因素。
items.example: The same silence can be interpreted as respect or uncertainty, depending on the context.

items.explanation: 与其做……，不如……。rather than 后接动名词时，用于对比两种做法，并推荐后者。
items.example: Rather than filling every pause, observe how others respond.

items.question: In unfamiliar situations, it is often best to ______ judgment until you have more context.
用 Rather than + doing... 改写：Do not assume silence means disagreement. Look for additional clues.
According to the passage, why can silence cause mistrust in cross-cultural communication?

sections.label: Check Your Work
sections.title: 答案
items: Rather than assuming silence means disagreement, look for additional clues.
Because the same silence can carry different or even opposite meanings, and people may mistakenly treat their own interpretation as universal or obvious.
